subject.title: fix(imessage): repair DM sender fallback before pairing

question: For non-group, not-from-me iMessage DMs whose sender canonicalizes to destination_caller_id, should OpenClaw drop the payload when no distinct canonical peer can be recovered before access control, or only repair confident peer cases?
rationale: That choice controls whether ambiguous local-sender payloads can reach authorization, pairing, routing, and reply delivery, so it is a security-boundary policy decision rather than only a mechanical refactor.

options.title: Repair canonical peers and drop ambiguous payloads
options.body: Use normalizeIMessageHandle for all comparisons, repair only a distinct canonical peer, and drop unresolved local-sender DMs before access control.

options.title: Repair only confident peers
options.body: Fix the canonicalization bug but preserve current pass-through behavior when no distinct peer is recoverable, accepting the residual identity risk.

options.title: Pause until the root cause is split
options.body: If the author's remaining failure is not this sender-fallback race, pause this branch and track the narrower iMessage identity issue separately.

recommendation.title: Repair canonical peers and drop ambiguous payloads
recommendation.body: Use normalizeIMessageHandle for all comparisons, repair only a distinct canonical peer, and drop unresolved local-sender DMs before access control.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged work established the destination_caller_id self-chat classification behavior this decision builds on.
